newsitem.title: USA: GM would keep 80 pct of Delco/Delphi spinoff.
newsitem.headline: GM would keep 80 pct of Delco/Delphi spinoff.

text.p: General Motors Corp. Chairman John Smith Jr. said Wednesday the automaker would likely retain about 80 percent of its combined Delco Electronics and Delphi Automotive Systems unit in any future spinoff.

Smith told reporters after a speech to the Economic Club of Detroit that the company needs several shareholder and government approvals to consolidate the two units before it can finalise plans of a future public offering.
Smith said the amount of ownership in Delphi/Delco that would be offered to the public at a future date "would not be more than 20 percent."

GM had said it would consider publicly offering an undisclosed stake in the giant automotive components operation last month when it announced the $9.5 billion sale of Hughes Electronics Corp.'s defence assets to Raytheon Co.

Hughes will survive the deal as a wholly owned telecommunications and satellite subsidiary. One of the things yet to be determined is how GM will reimburse its Class H shareholders for the shift of Delco Electronics from Hughes to Delphi, which is now part of GM's North American Operations.

He said one of the possible models for the company's future structure would be Japanese auto parts giant Denso Corp., formerly known as Nippondenso Co. Ltd., which is closely tied to Toyota Motor Corp., but sells to automakers worldwide.
"What we're talking about is a smart-parts, smart-systems Delphi," Smith said.
Smith added that certain core technologies or components now grouped in the two units may be excluded from the entity that is spun off. He declined to name any specific groups.
Smith did not offer a figure on how much GM expects to save by combining its Delco and Delphi Systems operations. But added that savings per vehicle could reach into the hundreds of dollars.
